🏭NUT INVENTORY & INFRASTRUCTURE
StocksPhysical chainCoverageRWASources
🏭 RWA · Stocks / custody / logistics

Inventory is the collateral layer.

Production tells us what was harvested. Trade tells us what crossed a border. Inventory asks what physically remains, in what form, under whose custody, and for how long.

38.969M lbShelled pecans · Dec 31 2025 [1]
60.126M lbIn-shell pecans · Dec 31 2025 [1]
256,877 MTGlobal almond ending stocks · MY2024/25 [2]
15.9%Almond stocks / domestic use · derived [2]
Critical distinctionAggregate stocks are market evidence, not proof of a lot.

Tokenized inventory still requires lot-level quantity, grade, location, legal control and audit evidence.

01 · STOCKS

What is actually reported

Pecans provide concrete monthly U.S. warehouse data. Almonds have strong annual FAS carryout data, but not the same standardized monthly cold-storage series.

02 · PHYSICAL CHAIN

From orchard to custody

Supply-chain content belongs here when the question is physical state, storage or control; cross-border movement stays on Nut Trade Flows.

QuantityMass

Exact lot weight and product state.

IdentityGrade

Variety, grade, shell state, crop year.

ControlCustody

Warehouse, owner, liens and release authority.

ConditionAge

Storage date, environment and inspection state.

03 · COVERAGE

The public-data boundary

Absence of data should remain visible rather than being replaced by inferred precision.

LayerStrengthBest sourceCan establishCannot establish
Pecan warehouse stocksStrongNASS monthlyAggregate shelled/in-shell warehouse stocksSpecific lot ownership or condition
Almond global ending stocksStrong annualFAS PSDCountry/global carryoutMonthly warehouse-level inventory
FacilitiesFragmentedBoards / firms / permitsKnown handlers and processorsComplete global capacity registry
Tokenizable lotPrivate evidenceCustodian + auditLot quantity/grade/locationCannot be inferred from national data
04 · RWA

A commodity claim needs a custody graph.

The minimum credible inventory primitive is a claim connected to a dated lot, product definition, custodian, quantity, inspection state, legal control and release mechanism.

ValuationStocks/use frames market tightness.
HaircutsAge, grade and liquidity matter.
VerificationOfficial aggregates cross-check audits.
LiquidationLinks to Trade Flows and Demand.

Why no separate “Supply Chain” page

The chain divides cleanly: Orchard Economics covers creation; this page covers processing, storage and custody; Trade Flows covers border movement; Demand covers absorption. A generic supply-chain page would duplicate those layers.

Sources

Data registry

Aggregate official inventory data validate the market around a lot; they do not prove custody of a specific lot.

[1] USDA NASS · Cold Storage · January 23, 2026 ↗Stocks in all warehouses: Dec. 31, 2024; Nov. 30, 2025; Dec. 31, 2025.
[2] USDA FAS · Tree Nuts: World Markets and Trade · October 2024 ↗Global almond ending stocks and domestic use, metric tons, shelled basis.
[3] USDA FAS · PSD Online ↗Machine-readable annual beginning/ending stocks by country and commodity.
[4] USDA NASS · Publications ↗Official entry point for current and historical NASS reports and Quick Stats/API access.
